title: Affine algebra adjunction preserves finite limits
statement: Let f:X→Y be an affine scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme]. Let g be the canonical morphism to the direct image algebra space (Y,f_* O_X) [def-sc-direct-image-algebra-derived-category], and let G=g_* be module direct image [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image] on module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume G is a right adjoint and use its canonical left adjoint and adjunction. Then the canonical left adjoint preserves finite limits. Quasi-coherence is the property of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-module-correspondence].

proof.text: Identify the canonical left adjoint with tensor pullback using the tensor Hom adjunction. On an affine open Spec B with inverse image Spec A, the stalk map at p over q is the localization A localized away from q to A_p, hence flat. Tensor pullback preserves kernels by the exact, jointly conservative stalk functors. It preserves finite products because tensor preserves finite direct sums. Kernels and finite products imply preservation of finite limits in an abelian category. Transport along the unique isomorphism of left adjoints. Empty schemes and zero modules cause no exceptions.
